solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: It may be the thing required

definitions.meaning: the word 'the' is the definite ... in grammar
an ... is an item or object, as in 'an ... of clothing'

explanation.surface: A vague definition of whatever object happens to be needed.
explanation.definitionFit: Grammar calls 'the' the definite article, and an item or object is also called an article.

clue.text: Pretend to influence

definitions.meaning: to ... an accent is to put it on, feigning
to have an effect on something

explanation.surface: Someone fakes a show in order to sway others.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb has two senses: to feign a manner, and to have an effect on something.

clue.text: A superior suit

parts.note: suit is a card suit, not clothing: the one nominated to beat all others in a hand

explanation.surface: Sounds like a smart bit of tailoring.
explanation.definitionFit: Trumps are the card suit that outranks every other suit in a hand.

clue.text: Plan to recycle liqueur

parts.note: a chart is a map or plan
to recycle something is to reuse it

explanation.surface: An instruction to make a plan for recycling a bottle of liqueur.
explanation.definitionFit: Chartreuse is a green or yellow French herbal liqueur made by Carthusian monks.

clue.text: Former tax reduced by a pound — celebrate

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife

indicators.note: the tax word is made smaller by taking away the pound sign

parts.note: a toll is a charge or tax levied for road use
L is the abbreviation for a pound sterling, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: A former levy has been cut by a pound, which is cause for celebration.
explanation.definitionFit: To extol is to praise highly, which is to celebrate someone or something.

clue.text: He swears he's a soldier

definitions.meaning: the idiom 'swear like a ...' makes this soldier a byword for bad language
a cavalry or armoured private soldier

explanation.surface: A foul-mouthed man turns out to be in the army.
explanation.definitionFit: A private cavalry soldier is a trooper, and the saying 'swear like a trooper' gives the first sense.

clue.text: Where to see the beginning — and end — of the rainbow?

definitions.text: Where to see the beginning — and end — of the rainbow?

parts.words: Where to see the beginning — and end — of the rainbow?
parts.note: rainbow trout are bred and finally killed at a fish farm, so the rainbow is a fish, not an arc of colour

explanation.surface: A whimsical question about where a rainbow starts and stops.
explanation.definitionFit: Rainbow trout are hatched and raised for the table at a fish farm devoted to that species.

clue.text: Give marching orders to us to put out

indicators.note: put out suggests the letters are disturbed and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is told to expel us and throw us out.
explanation.definitionFit: To give someone their marching orders is to dismiss or expel them.

clue.text: Capital turn of a pierrot

indicators.note: a turn here is a twisting round, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A pierrot clown's act, a turn, performed in some capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Pretoria is the administrative capital city of South Africa.

clue.text: It aids digestion if having hard time

parts.note: rough means hard or harsh
an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: Something helps the gut if you are going through a tough period.
explanation.definitionFit: Dietary fibre, also called roughage, helps food move through the gut.

clue.text: Goat-like figure heads a list of animals

indicators.note: heads means the first piece goes in front of the next

parts.note: a faun is a Roman woodland god, half man and half goat

explanation.surface: A satyr-like creature tops a catalogue of creatures.
explanation.definitionFit: Fauna is the whole animal life of a region, as catalogued in a list of species.

clue.text: Not a single female will go out in this outfit

definitions.text: Not a single female will go out in this outfit

parts.words: Not a single female will go out in this outfit
parts.note: a bride, no longer a single woman, sets off with the clothes she has gathered for married life

explanation.surface: Seems to say that no woman would be seen dead in these clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: A bride's collection of clothes and linen for her marriage is her trousseau.

clue.text: Give up using catapult — i.e. playing around

indicators.note: playing around suggests the letters are fooled with and rearranged

explanation.surface: Surrender while messing about with a slingshot.
explanation.definitionFit: To capitulate is to surrender, to give in or yield to an opponent.

clue.text: High-class sort of shop

indicators.note: to sort is to arrange, so the letters of the next word are rearranged

explanation.surface: A description of an upmarket kind of store.
explanation.definitionFit: Posh is informal British English for smart, upper-class or elegant.

clue.text: Racketeers' go-between?

parts.note: racketeers here are players with rackets, and what passes between them on court is a ball

explanation.surface: Suggests a middleman for gangsters.
explanation.definitionFit: A tennis ball travels back and forth between the two racket-wielding players.

clue.text: We need to find our own fare for these holidays

definitions.text: We need to find our own fare for these holidays

parts.words: We need to find our own fare for these holidays
parts.note: fare is food, not a ticket price; on these holidays guests cook their own meals

explanation.surface: Holidaymakers complain that they must pay their own travel costs.
explanation.definitionFit: Self-catering holidays provide accommodation with a kitchen, and guests supply their own food.

clue.text: She parts company with an angler

indicators.note: the first word splits the company word apart by sitting inside it

parts.note: a firm is a business company

explanation.surface: A woman leaves a fishing enthusiast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'parts company' looks like an idiom for splitting up, but 'parts' is the container signal working on the business word, and 'with' just joins.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who fishes with rod and line is an angler, a kind of fisher.

clue.text: Take care — if it changed, it's a trick

indicators.note: changed signals that the letters are altered in order

explanation.surface: A warning to watch out, since if something has been altered it is a con.
explanation.definitionFit: An artifice is a clever trick or deceptive device.

clue.text: Don't stand round showing what a bad crack will do

definitions.meaning: to land full length rather than stay upright

definitions.text: what a bad crack will do
definitions.meaning: a crack is a joke, and a poor one fails to get a laugh

explanation.surface: A warning about a fissure that could make something collapse.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means both to tumble prone and, of a joke, to fail to amuse.

clue.text: Turbulent masses resent another property valuation

indicators.note: turbulent means stirred up, so the letters are disturbed

explanation.surface: Angry crowds object to a revaluation of their homes.
explanation.definitionFit: Assessing a property's value again is a fresh appraisal of it.

clue.text: Old court official, specifically one over the Queen

indicators.note: in a down clue over means placed above the next piece

parts.note: viz is short for videlicet, namely or specifically
I is the Roman numeral for one
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: Names a particular courtier who outranks the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: A vizier was a high official at the court of a Muslim ruler, as in the Ottoman Empire.

clue.text: Guarantee Rex is about to succeed? Quite the opposite

indicators.note: is about suggests one piece going round another
this reverses the roles stated, so the follow-on word goes round the king's letter

parts.note: to ensue is to follow on, to succeed
R is the abbreviation for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: Asks whether a king is on the verge of success.
explanation.walkthrough: Read plainly, R would go round ENSUE; 'Quite the opposite' swaps the roles so ENSUE holds R.
explanation.definitionFit: To ensure something is to make sure of it, to guarantee it.

clue.text: Lazy, appearing backward in fielding

indicators.note: appearing backward means the found letters are read right to left
in shows the letters sit inside the next word

explanation.surface: A cricketer slacking while fielding.
explanation.definitionFit: Idle means lazy, not inclined to work.

clue.text: Slump causing gloom

explanation.surface: An economic downturn leaves everyone miserable.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both a severe economic downturn and a state of deep sadness.

clue.text: Limit the area for stock

definitions.meaning: the extent or limits within which something varies

explanation.surface: Fencing off where livestock may roam.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both the scope or limits of something and open land where cattle graze.

clue.text: Served up in Norway, osprey is a source of protein

indicators.note: Served up says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A Norwegian bird of prey dished up as a protein-rich meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Soya beans are rich in protein and widely eaten as a meat substitute.

clue.text: Starting place for the three-legged race?

definitions.text: Starting place for the three-legged race?

parts.words: Starting place for the three-legged race?
parts.note: race means a people, not a contest: the triskelion of three legs is the emblem of this island's inhabitants

explanation.surface: Asks where the sports-day three-legged race begins.
explanation.walkthrough: The Isle of Man is a self-governing island in the Irish Sea whose flag shows three legs joined at the hip.
explanation.definitionFit: The three-legged triskelion is the national symbol of the Manx people, so their homeland is where that race starts.

clue.text: Something cast in gold — the last word in France

indicators.note: in puts the cast object inside the gold symbol

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
a die is something cast, as in 'the die is cast'

explanation.surface: A golden casting is the final word on French style.
explanation.definitionFit: Adieu is French for farewell, the last thing said on parting.

clue.text: Board carriage herd aren't in

indicators.note: to herd is to drive together and jumble, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Getting on a train where the cattle are not.
explanation.definitionFit: To entrain is to get aboard a train, boarding its carriage.

clue.text: Increase in general disorder

indicators.note: disorder signals the letters are put out of order

explanation.surface: Chaos in the army growing widespread.
explanation.definitionFit: To enlarge something is to make it bigger, to increase it.
